Fleet exposes current operational work and attention state; Supervision exposes exact source-bound MC-only reasoning ownership and workflow state; infrastructure health projects authenticated shared-authority, host, queue, pacing, cooldown, and ledger evidence without private identifiers. The live deployment contains no misleading demo workers, remains loopback-private behind owner SSH access, and worker/browser/clipboard execution remains on the VPS topology.

required_outcomes.observable: One concise, stable, live-tested owner procedure opens the loopback-private Mission Control dashboard without public exposure or credential disclosure.
The deployed Fleet root and worker detail pages show current live workers/tasks and attention state rather than demo or fixture workers; authenticated reads and SSE live updates work.

The deployed Supervision view derives transport health from current authenticated Mission Control and submission-authority evidence, removing static NOT_CONNECTED and stale pre-live transport copy and failing closed when evidence is unavailable.

The permanent Project Manager and specialist MC-only chats are shown with registered, reachable, and source-bound state, current task ownership, latest verified reasoning age, and direct private Open Chat controls without exposing locators in logs or repository state.

Fleet and Supervision plainly distinguish running, parked, attention, failed, waiting-for-reasoning, executing, awaiting-evidence, finished, pending supervisor routes, and owner-decision waits with current action and next review trigger.

A compact live health area shows active host role and epoch, authority and per-host worker/browser health, queue depth, last boundary, configured/recent/minimum pacing, violations, cooldown/rate-limit state, and ledger integrity without secrets or private target identifiers.
Owner viewing remains separate from execution: no Mission Control worker, controller, browser automation, or clipboard operation returns to Joel's workstation.
The exact deployed candidate passes applicable repository, Mission Control, relay, authentication/security, build, live access/view, review, and hosted merge checks.
